McLaren.summary: McLaren has tweaked the rear‑corner airflow by reshaping the brake‑duct inlet, giving the car cleaner, more consistent cooling and a bit more rear‑end grip. They’ve also adjusted the rear‑wing flap to a “straight‑line” setting, shaving off drag so the car can hit higher top speeds on the long straights. Together, these changes should help McLaren get a stronger launch off the line and better stability through the high‑speed sections of this weekend’s track.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has tweaked the shape of the front‑track fairings to smooth the air around the front wheels, giving the car a bit more front‑end grip and stability on the straights and into corners. They’ve also narrowed the rear opening of the engine cover, improving cooling efficiency while shaving off a little drag. Together these changes should help the team keep the tires in the sweet spot and maintain better pace over the weekend’s high‑speed sections.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have reshaped the side‑pod inlet and matching engine‑cover panels to tidy up the airflow and stop the little reliability gremlins that have been popping up.  At the same time, subtle tweaks to the floor, diffuser, rear‑suspension fairings and wing pylons tighten the car’s rear‑end aerodynamics, giving the car more bite and steadier grip through the corners.  Finally, a lower‑mounted exhaust with a new bracket smooths the rear‑flow plume, helping to extract a touch more power and stability for this weekend’s track.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari’s aero package gets a subtle but important clean‑up for this weekend: the front wing now sports a reshaped end‑plate with a new dive‑plane and re‑ordered foot‑vane, giving the car a bit more front‑end grip and stability on the straights. At the rear, they’ve taken off the central RV‑tail fin, and the floor has been simplified to a single vertical element, both aimed at reducing drag and improving rear‑wheel balance. Finally, a shorter mirror stalk tucked into the side‑pod trims the car’s side‑profile, shaving off a little extra drag and helping the overall package run smoother through fast corners.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has reshaped the airflow at the front corner of the car to smooth the air and give the front end a bit more grip, while also fine‑tuning the cooling louvers to match the circuit’s temperature range. The result should be a more stable, responsive car out of the first turn and a better‑kept‑together power unit, helping the team extract a few extra tenths on the weekend.

Audi F1 Team.summary: Audi’s F1 car gets a sweeping aerodynamic tidy‑up this weekend: the front‑wing endplates and lower deflector, plus a reshaped lower beam wing and rear‑wing, have all been refined to give cleaner airflow and a steadier down‑force balance. The floor, rear‑corner deflector and rear suspension have also been re‑profiled to boost rear‑end grip without upsetting the car’s stability. In short, the updates should make the car feel more planted in high‑speed corners and give the drivers a little extra confidence on the straights and under braking.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has rolled out a fresh front‑wing package – new wing, endplates and nose – plus a reshaped front‑corner area and a small winglet on the diffuser. The changes tighten up the car’s front grip and clean up the airflow, giving the driver more stability and a little extra downforce into the corners. In short, the car should feel more planted and quicker around this weekend’s track, especially in the high‑speed and braking zones.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac’s new kit opens up the car’s “breathing passages” – a bigger, reshaped side‑pod inlet and revamped engine‑cover fins let the power unit stay cooler while shaving off drag, so the car can push harder for longer. The front‑floor and diffuser have been re‑contoured, and the beam wing and roll‑hoop fairings reshaped, tightening the airflow under and over the car for extra rear‑end grip when it’s on the throttle. In short, the package gives Cadillac a cooler, more stable platform that should translate into quicker lap times and a stronger fight for podium spots this weekend.
